classification.difficultyReason: Construct the surrounding-square model, recognise that the width adds twice to each outer dimension, and subtract hut area before solving.

content.prompt:
A square hut with side length 5 metres is to be surrounded by a veranda of width $x$ metres.
Find the width of the veranda if the area of the veranda is $24\text{ m}^2$. (Hint: draw a diagram first)

answer.worked:
The outer square has side length $(5+2x)$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}(2x+5)(2x+5)-24&=5\times5\\4x^2+20x+25-24&=25\\4x^2+20x-24&=0\\x^2+5x-6&=0\\(x+6)(x-1)&=0\\x&=-6\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
Since $x>0$, the veranda is $1\text{ m}$ wide.
Check: $7^2-5^2=24\text{ m}^2$.
